claims.text: Local atomic environments and lattice distortions largely determine phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
The relevant lattice distortions arise from atomic-mass, size, and electronegativity mismatches.
A model that explicitly quantifies local chemical fluctuations will identify low-lattice-thermal-conductivity high-entropy alloys more accurately than models based only on average or bulk parameters.
FeCoCrMnNi is an example of a five-element high-entropy alloy relevant to the proposed approach.
The proposed initial alloy has moderate lattice distortions.
A metallic high-entropy alloy such as FeCoCrMnNi has been considered for ambient-condition thermal-insulation applications.
First-principles calculations or machine-learned force fields can quantify local chemical and strain-field fluctuations for use as predictive descriptors.
Local-disorder descriptors can be used to predict enhanced phonon scattering and lower thermal conductivity.
Force-constant fluctuations associated with local lattice distortion intensify phonon scattering and shorten phonon mean free paths.
Local disorder lowers phonon velocities.
Local disorder shortens phonon lifetimes.
Reduced phonon velocity and increased phonon scattering decrease intrinsic lattice thermal conductivity.
Explicitly representing local disorder makes the approach superior to models that average out local effects.
For alloys with pronounced local lattice distortions, the new approach will forecast significantly lower phonon thermal conductivity than conventional models.
Alloys classified by the approach as low-κL will exhibit lower measured lattice thermal conductivity than baseline predictions.
The approach is applicable only to high-entropy alloys with at least four principal elements and significant mass, size, or electronegativity differences.
The model's predictive advantage diminishes when constituent properties are nearly homogeneous.
Extreme porosity or secondary-phase precipitation can dominate thermal transport and diminish the model's predictive advantage.
The model can be assessed by measuring lattice thermal conductivity over temperature and comparing its predictions with conventional averaged models.

Failure to achieve closer agreement with measured lattice thermal conductivity than conventional models, or failure of predicted low-κL alloys to show statistically lower values, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is computational and only quantifies existing fluctuations, whereas the structural mediator is phrased as an enhancement of the alloy's lattice distortions. The model does not itself physically increase distortion.
